A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLIM research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison; appendix renumbering and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original zero-shot accuracy, WikiText2 perplexity, GPU speedup, compression-cost, and sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds MaskLLM comparisons, input-quantization evaluations, an alternative quantization-objective comparison, and measured GPU memory results.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 adds SLIM-QuantO, an activation-aware variant that selects salient channels using activation and weight magnitudes, scales their weights, and inversely scales their inputs. This extends the quantization procedure while retaining the original quantizer as SLIM-QuantW and preserving the principal pruning and low-rank pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six zero-shot benchmarks, WikiText2 language modeling, and C4/SlimPajama calibration data. The added experiments change compression configurations within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Table 3 adds MaskLLM, both without quantization and with Group AbsMax, as a comparator for Naive-LoRA and SLIM-LoRA combinations. Existing comparator sets remain. Newly discussed OATS, QERA, and CALDERA are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V3 adds configurations combining 4-bit weights with 8-bit inputs, comparisons using MaskLLM masks, and A100 memory measurements. The existing calibration count, fine-tuning budget, adapter-rank default, and GPU timing batch sizes remain unchanged. No corresponding protocol revision is stated for the updated existing scores.

E4.justification: V3 adds focused input-quantization robustness tests in Tables 5 and 12, compares weight-error and output-aware quantization in Table 6, and breaks down speedup contributions from quantization and sparsity. Earlier rank, calibration-sample, calibration-dataset, and sparsity-ratio analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or formal significance tests. V3 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results are substantially expanded and revised. Table 1 changes JSQ's 2:4 LLaMA-2-7B accuracy from 45.34 to 44.80. V2 Table 8 versus v3 Table 10 changes SLIM-LoRA perplexity from 7.56 to 7.77. A100 7B up-projection speedup with batch 16 and FP16 adapters changes from 0.85× to 2.2×. New MaskLLM, input-quantization, objective-comparison, and memory results supplement these revisions.

T1.justification: V3 introduces a channel-saliency definition using normalized average activation and weight magnitudes for SLIM-QuantO. The original quantization derivation, invertibility/additivity argument, SVD construction, and resource-analysis equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract adds a reported 0.23× end-to-end memory figure and updates the claimed RTX3060 peak speedup from 3.78× to 4.3×. The principal claims about one-shot joint compression, saliency-based adapters, and accuracy benefits remain.

C2.justification: V3 interprets input quantization as robust and discusses SLIM-QuantO's accuracy versus inference-overhead tradeoff, although Table 6 shows mixed accuracy changes. It removes v2 Appendix H's explicit A100 slowdown caveat even though v3 Figure 4 still contains speedups below 1×.

D1.justification: New details specify approximately 1% salient-channel scaling and per-tensor AbsMax scaling with E4M3/E5M2 format selection. Existing implementation settings and code/data access information remain. Appendix B ambiguously calls FP8 weight quantization despite Table 5 specifying 4-bit weights and 8-bit inputs.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion of MaskLLM, OATS, QERA, CALDERA, training-time sparsity, and sparsity–quantization interplay. It replaces v2's characterization of L2QER as the only zero-shot low-rank comparator with broader recognition of concurrent methods, while retaining SLIM's positioning around joint sparsity and quantization.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain intact. V3 adds local method and experiment passages, two appendix sections, and an Impact Statement; it also updates headings, cross-references, notation terminology, affiliations, and the publication header.

P2.justification: V2's RTX3060 speedup Table 3 becomes v3's breakdown Figure 3, and the A100 plot is redrawn as Figure 4 with revised axes and component shading. V3 also adds the MaskLLM table and three appendix tables, substantially expanding and revising the experimental displays. Other figures and tables are retained with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V3 directly supports the memory-efficiency argument with A100 measurements and strengthens practical validation through input-quantization, objective-choice, and MaskLLM tests. These provide a limited overall improvement. Benefits are tempered by unexplained numerical revisions, the overly favorable interpretation of mixed Table 6 results, and removal of the A100 slowdown caveat despite remaining sub-1× results.
